posts.title: Planning Ahead: A Reading Program for 2027
posts.description: Most years around this time I start thinking about the year to come, a consequence as much of exhaustion with the work I have on my immediate to-do list as anything else. Next year is pregnant with possibility that this year has nearly exhausted. There is still a month left in 2026 and I have no intention of prematurely writing my annual retrospective series, but I have had several recent conversations that made it clear to me the topic I should choose for my semi-regular annual academic reading theme (this is too wordy to serve as a reasonable name for the project). This is a semi-regular practice where I choose a topic related to an upcoming elective and refresh my familiarity with the scholarly literature by creating a reading list on that theme. In 2022, for instance, I chose Roman History , in 2023 I picked a broad-spectrum Food History , and in 2025 I created a long list of World History titles for a Graduate readings course I taught. posts.title: First Snow 2026
posts.description: Taking a page from Bill Caraher’s playbook (again) to mark the first snow of the season here in Northeast Missouri. I only have a few shots because my dog is a princess who objected to the cold and the wet and the wintery mix that is intermittently falling, thus cutting our walk short today. I will take her out again later, but the temperatures having been hovering around freezing this morning and the daytime temperatures could melt it all away. Still, this is unquestionably our first snow of the season, and as good an excuse as the holiday to make my favorite dinner roll recipe (which we will be serving with our decidedly new world but untraditional meal of chili). Happy Thanksgiving!

posts.title: Weekly Varia no. 209, 11/22/26
posts.description: I am having a hard time processing that the semester is nearly over. The week before break passed more or less as normal, right down to attendance. My Friday classes had more absences from students traveling to Big Rapids, Michigan, to perform with the marching band for the playoff game against Ferris State featured on Fox’s Big Noon Saturday as I did from students leaving early for break. This is not to say that the building wasn’t noticeably quiet on Friday afternoon, but my classes were mostly full. By the time we return next week we will be in the last week of the semester. After the gauntlet that this semester has been, this is an abrupt stop moderated only by the grading I have left and next semester’s classes that I need to prepare. Of course, I spent the first weekend of break doing precisely nothing from either category.
